original_question: Determine whether the sequence {sqrt(k)/k!}_{k>=0} is a multiplier sequence and whether it is a complex zero decreasing sequence. Equivalently for the first part, decide whether the entire function phi(x)=sum_{k>=0} sqrt(k) x^k/(k!k!) belongs to the Laguerre-Polya class with nonnegative coefficients.
target_in_paper: Problem 5 in Section 5: determine whether the specific sequence {√k/k!}_{k=0}^∞ is (a) a multiplier sequence and (b) a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS). The first half is foreshadowed in Section 3.1 by the conjectural question whether φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2 lies in the Laguerre-Pólya class with nonnegative coefficients.

It is therefore very close to the paper’s actual target, especially Problem 5 and the Section 3.1 conjectural discussion.

To make the question stand-alone, the multiplier-sequence part should define the diagonal operator T on ℝ[x] by T[x^k]=γ_k x^k with γ_k=√k/k!, and state that T must send every real polynomial with only real zeros to another such polynomial.

To make the CZDS part stand-alone, one must define it exactly as in Definition 3: Z_C(T[p])≤Z_C(p) for every real polynomial p∈ℝ[x], where Z_C(p) is the number of nonreal zeros of p counted with multiplicity.
The universal quantifier is over all real polynomials p(x)∈ℝ[x]; there are no degree, homogeneity, or characteristic restrictions in this problem.
The index set should be made explicit as k=0,1,2,…, so γ_0=0.

The first-part equivalence should be stated precisely via Pólya-Schur Theorem 2(iii): the sequence is a multiplier sequence iff ∑_{k=0}^∞ γ_k x^k/k! belongs to the Laguerre-Pólya class of type I; because γ_k≥0, Definition 2 identifies this with the Laguerre-Pólya class with nonnegative coefficients.
The equivalence applies only to part (a), not to the CZDS part.

If one wants the nearby paper-faithful context, Section 3.1 notes numerical evidence, Lemma 11 proves Hurwitz stability of φ, and Theorem 12 gives integral representations, but these are supporting context rather than part of the official statement.
refined_question: Let γ_k:=√k/k! for k=0,1,2,…. Determine whether the diagonal operator T:ℝ[x]→ℝ[x] defined by T[x^k]=γ_k x^k is (i) a classical multiplier sequence, meaning that T[p] has only real zeros whenever the real polynomial p has only real zeros, and (ii) a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS), meaning that Z_C(T[p])≤Z_C(p) for every p∈ℝ[x], where Z_C counts nonreal zeros with multiplicity.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation for part (i) only: by Theorem 2(iii), determine whether the entire function φ(x)=∑_{k=0}^∞ (√k/k!) x^k/k! = ∑_{k=0}^∞ √k x^k/(k!)^2 belongs to the Laguerre-Pólya class of type I; since all coefficients are nonnegative, this is the same as asking whether φ belongs to the Laguerre-Pólya class with nonnegative coefficients.
justification: The exact paper target matching both parts of your draft is Problem 5 in Section 5. Your first clause is also exactly the Section 3.1 question phrased there as the unresolved membership of φ(x)=∑_{k≥0}√k x^k/(k!)^2 in the Laguerre-Pólya class with nonnegative coefficients. To make the problem fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the definitions of multiplier sequence and CZDS must be imported from Definition 4 and Definition 3, respectively, with the operator acting on ℝ[x]. The reformulation of only the multiplier-sequence half follows from the Pólya-Schur characterization in Theorem 2(iii), together with Definition 2 for the notation involving nonnegative coefficients. Lemma 11 and Theorem 12 are the nearby contextual results the paper supplies around this sequence: they show that φ is Hurwitz stable and provide integral representations, which explain the paper’s interest in the problem without changing its scope.
